_doc: First system2 case (ticket #12). Tests time-domain tools (schedule_meeting) with a reasoning-heavy prompt: user gives a meeting in UTC and asks for the equivalent local time in another zone. The `system` field carries the 'think first' instruction (per the #4 amendment of 2026-10-07) — the model does not emit <thought> by default on the chat-completions endpoint, but does emit reliably when nudged. require_thought: true. Note: only `schedule_meeting` is exposed; the other time tools (get_current_time, cancel_meeting, list_calendar) were dropped from the tool list because the v3 4-bit model's output budget runs out before it can emit the call when 4 detailed schemas are present. With 1 tool, thought + call fit in 512 tokens.
_loader_note: TODO for ticket #19 (Hermes FC adapter): when the case loader enumerates evals/hermes_fc/cases/*.json, skip this file. The case is staged here for the probe record and will move to the cases branch when fc-system2-002..005 are authored. Until then, listing it will double-count it once the cases branch lands.
_probe_note: Probe scenario: user gives a meeting time in one timezone and asks the result in another. The model has to reason about the offset to pick the right 'time' + 'timezone' values. A well-reasoning model will emit a <thought> block before the tool call; this case is the gate for the System-2 scoring rule from #4. NOTE: 2026-11-04 is EST (UTC-5) because DST ends 2026-11-01, so 14:00 UTC = 09:00 America/New_York. The `system` field carries the 'think first' instruction (per the #4 amendment of 2026-10-07) — the model does not emit <thought> by default on the chat-completions endpoint, but does emit reliably when nudged.
prompt: I have a 30-minute meeting planned with bob@example.com at 14:00 UTC on 2026-11-04. Re-schedule it to the equivalent local time in America/New_York on the same date. Keep the duration at 30 minutes and keep Bob as the only attendee. Use the title 'meeting with Bob'.
system: Before answering, write your reasoning inside a <thought>...</thought> block. Then call the tool using the <tool_call> format.

function.name: schedule_meeting
function.description: Schedule a calendar meeting. `attendees` is a list of email addresses, `date` is YYYY-MM-DD, `time` is HH:MM in 24h, `timezone` is an IANA tz like 'Europe/London', `duration_minutes` is an integer.
